why_a_sidecar: protocol/v1.json and protocol/v2.json both declare themselves frozen and byte-immutable after their landing task, so the bounds that the exploratory runner enforces are declared here instead of being edited into a frozen file. Nothing in this file changes a metric, tolerance, parameter, control, integrator or decision rule: the baseline still loads its parameters from the protocol version it names, and this file only bounds which explicitly labelled exploratory deviations the runner will accept.

exploration.baseline_source: the named protocol version's model.parameters and numerics.solver_settings

alpha.note: alpha=0 is control C1's linear chain; alpha=1.0 is the report's Fig. 2 condition. No digitization exists for Fig. 2, so an alpha!=0.25 run is a qualitative comparison only.

dt.note: The baseline is dt=1/sqrt(8)=0.3535533905932738 because the caption states delta t^2=1/8. dt=0.125 is the naive reading of the caption and is allowed only as an exploratory run; it moves the recurrence far outside the 30,000-cycle window.

cycles.note: A shortened or lengthened budget is diagnostic only. Metrics whose windows are not covered report pass: null rather than a tuned value.

rules: Only the keys listed above may be set; any other key is a usage error (exit code 2).
A value outside its declared range is refused with a message naming the key, the value and the allowed range (exit code 2).

Every exploratory run is written to its own explore-<delta-hash>-<timestamp> directory with kind: exploratory, baseline_eligible: false and the parameter delta against the named protocol recorded in run.json.
An exploratory run never writes to, relabels or deletes a baseline run directory, and never becomes the registered baseline.

changelog.change: Added the exploration bounds block for alpha, dt and cycles as a separate sidecar file rather than editing protocol/v1.json (which the task suggested) or protocol/v2.json, because both declare themselves frozen and immutable after landing.
changelog.reason: The runner must validate exploratory parameter ranges against a declared protocol artifact rather than hard-coded constants, without touching any normative term or the digests that existing runs and scientific records pin.
